req.title: Create form GET returns 200
req.statement: The system shall serve the create-post form at GET /create for authenticated users.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-038 requires GET /create to return HTTP 200 for authenticated users. Three test cases are needed: (1) positive — authenticated user gets 200; (2) negative — unauthenticated user is redirected (not 200); (3) boundary — session state transition from unauthenticated to authenticated then GET /create returns exactly 200. Each test uses exact status-code assertions to kill comparison-operator mutations (== vs >=, 200 vs 302). The negative test asserts the redirect status is exactly 302 and the Location header points to /auth/login, killing constant and string mutations. The boundary/STC test verifies the state transition: before login the response is 302, after login it is exactly 200, catching any off-by-one or boolean-negation mutation in login_required.

tests.name: test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database containing seeded users
User is logged in via POST /auth/login
expected: Response body contains the create-post form (b'create' or b'Create' present)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/create')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'create' in r.data.lower() or b'Create' in r.data

test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200()

tests.name: test_create_get_state_transition_unauth_then_auth
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database containing seeded users
actions: POST /auth/login with username='Anjali' and password='cloud' — expect 302
trace: R-FLASKR-038: state transition unauthenticated->authenticated->unauthenticated; only authenticated state yields 200
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_create_get_state_transition_unauth_then_auth():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r_before = client.get('/create')
    assert r_before.status_code == 302
    assert r_before.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r_auth = client.get('/create')
    assert r_auth.status_code == 200
    logout_r = client.post('/auth/logout')
    assert logout_r.status_code == 302
    r_after = client.get('/create')
    assert r_after.status_code == 302
    assert r_after.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_create_get_state_transition_unauth_then_auth()

Client attempts login with wrong password 'wrongpass'
actions: GET /create — session should still be unauthenticated
expected: Login response status is 200 (form re-rendered with error, not redirected)

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_create_get_wrong_password_still_unauthenticated():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'wrongpass'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Incorrect password.' in login_r.data
    r = client.get('/create')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
